title: Weil equivariance of the completed coefficient duality
statement:
Use the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and a finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside the fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $g_X$ be its geometric-Frobenius automorphism. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, use the bounded constructible pro-etale coefficient categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:Lg_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Put $\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ and $D_{X,\Lambda}=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$, using the constructible exceptional adjoint and coefficient-passage operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Duality sends Weil complexes contravariantly to Weil complexes. Its evaluation $K\otimes^L_\Lambda D_{X,\Lambda}K\to\omega_{X,\Lambda}$ and canonical biduality isomorphism $\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,\Lambda}D_{X,\Lambda}K$ are Weil equivariant. For every separated finite-type $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ on the geometric fibers lifts to Weil pairs, with equivariant unit and counit. For each finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset L\subset\Qlb$, the canonical dualizing and duality comparisons
$$
\omega_{X,E}\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,L},\qquad
(D_{X,E}K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,L}(K\otimes_E L)
$$
are Weil equivariant, as are their evaluation, biduality and exceptional-adjunction compatibility diagrams; their images in the common-stage $\Qlb$ category have the same property. These assertions use the rational Frobenius isomorphism itself and require no Frobenius-stable integral lattice.

proof.text: Work first at a finite coefficient field $E$. Write $\mathcal C_T=D^b_c(T,E)$ for a geometric fiber $T$, $P_T=Lg_T^*$, $F_f=Rf_!$, and $G_f=Rf^!$. By [thm-coef-rational-verdier], $D_T$ is an anti-equivalence of the actual rationalized constructible category, with its actual evaluation and invertible double-dual map. By [lem-coef-rational-operations], $D_T=R\mathcal Hom_E(-,\omega_T)$, $\omega_T=G_{a_T}E$, and $F_f\dashv G_f$ is an adjunction on these categories. In particular every internal Hom of the form $R\mathcal Hom_E(K,\omega_T)$ used below is bounded constructible. This supplies the preservation hypotheses needed to apply the internal-Hom and evaluation assertions of [lem-fix-weil-operations]; it does not assert an ambient exceptional right adjoint.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1, first two sentences: actual constructible domains

proof.text: The inverse of geometric Frobenius is again a scheme automorphism. The exact inverse-image equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] and the identification with derived pullback on integral constructible objects in [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] give mutually inverse pullback functors for $g_T$ and $g_T^{-1}$; their inverse identities rationalize by the morphism formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], so $P_T$ is an equivalence. For a morphism $f$ descended from $k_0$, its Frobenius square is Cartesian, and after giving the source corners the $k$-structures $a_Xg_X$ and $a_Yg_Y$ all arrows are separated finite-type $k$-morphisms. The coefficient categories do not depend on that choice of $k$-structure. The compact-support exchange is therefore invertible by [lem-coef-frobenius-exchange-equivalence], and the pullback tensor comparison preserves symmetry, associators and units by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso].

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: Frobenius comparison and its inverse; paragraph 2: internal Hom for an equivalence

proof.text:
Construct the exceptional comparison for the actual constructible adjunction, rather than invoking the ambient-admissible clause of [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Put $S=P_X$, $T=P_Y$, $F=F_f$, $G=G_f$, and let $\eta,\varepsilon$ be the unit and counit of [lem-coef-rational-operations]. With $a=a_f:TF\to FS$, take the mate of $a^{-1}$:
$$b:SG\xrightarrow{\eta SG}GFSG\xrightarrow{G a^{-1}G}GTFG\xrightarrow{GT\varepsilon}GT.$$
This is the mate defined in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with both adjunctions equal to $F\dashv G$, with its $G=S$, its $G'=T$, and its $\theta=a^{-1}$. Step 2 supplies both equivalences, so $b$ is invertible. Define $\theta_{GM}=G(\theta_M)b_M$. Naturality of $b$ gives the Weil-morphism equation for $G(u)$. Expanding the displayed mate and using the two triangle identities gives
$$(Ga)(bF)(S\eta)=\eta S,\qquad (\varepsilon T)(Fb)(aG)=T\varepsilon.$$
Multiplication by $GF(\theta_K)$ in the first and by $\theta_M$ in the second, followed by naturality of $\eta,\varepsilon$, gives exactly equivariance of $K\to GFK$ and $FGM\to M$. In particular apply this construction to $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the geometric fiber of $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. The constant coefficient object has its canonical pullback identification, so this gives the Weil isomorphism $\theta_\omega:P_X\omega_X\to\omega_X$. No ambient admissibility is imposed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: dualizing Weil structure; paragraph 3, last sentence: exceptional units and counits

proof.text:
Let $(K,\theta_K)$ be a Weil pair in the sense of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Apply the canonical internal-Hom Weil structure and equivariant evaluation of [lem-fix-weil-operations] to the pair $(K,\omega_X)$, whose Hom lies in the constructible category by Step 1. If $h:P_XR\mathcal Hom(K,\omega_X)\to R\mathcal Hom(P_XK,P_X\omega_X)$ is the comparison, this gives
$$\theta_{DK}=R\mathcal Hom(\theta_K^{-1},\theta_\omega)h
=D(\theta_K^{-1})c_K:P_XDK\xrightarrow{\sim}DK,$$
where $c_K=R\mathcal Hom(1,\theta_\omega)h:P_XDK\to D(P_XK)$. For a Weil morphism $u:K\to L$, the equation $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_Xu$ rearranges to $P_Xu\,\theta_K^{-1}=\theta_L^{-1}u$. Contravariant functoriality of internal Hom and naturality of $h$ then give $D(u)\theta_{DL}=\theta_{DK}P_XD(u)$. Thus $D$ is a contravariant functor on Weil pairs. Write $e_K:K\otimes DK\to\omega_X$. The evaluation clause of [lem-fix-weil-operations] gives the explicit equation
$$e_K(\theta_K\otimes\theta_{DK})\mu_{K,DK}=\theta_\omega P_X(e_K).$$
Here precomposition by $\theta_K^{-1}$ cancels evaluation on $\theta_K$; all Frobenius maps have degree zero, so the usual signed tensor symmetry is respected.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1, displayed dual Weil structure, and paragraph 2: evaluation and rational Frobenius

proof.text: The completed and rational tensor-Hom transpose bijection needed here and in Step 7 is [lem-coef-completed-tensor-hom-transpose]. It applies to the constructible objects from Step 1 with $Q=\omega_X$ and $P=K$ or $DK$. By [thm-coef-integral-verdier] and [thm-coef-rational-verdier], the actual biduality map is evaluation-defined and characterized by $$e_{DK}(1_{DK}\otimes\delta_K)=e_K\tau_{DK,K}.$$ Taking the transposes of the two sides of $\delta_K\theta_K=\theta_{DDK}P_X\delta_K$ after precomposition by $\theta_{DK}\otimes1_{P_XK}$ gives $$e_K(\theta_K\otimes\theta_{DK})\tau_{P_XDK,P_XK}$$ and $$e_{DK}(\theta_{DK}\otimes\theta_{DDK})(1\otimes P_X\delta_K).$$ Step 4 and symmetry compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identify these composites. The transpose bijection gives the equality, and invertibility of $\delta_K$ gives equivariance of its inverse.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: expanded transposition argument for biduality

proof.text: We next check the coefficient comparisons on which the passage to $\Qlb$ depends. Let $E\subset L$ be finite, $R=\mathcal O_E$, $S=\mathcal O_L$, and $e=e(L/E)$. At the cofinal quotient levels $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$, $B_n=S/\varpi_E^nS=S/\varpi_L^{en}$, [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] states that the scalar comparisons are natural under scheme isomorphisms, in particular geometric Frobenius with its base automorphism, and explicitly defines their maps by scalar tensor, evaluation and adjunction counits. Thus their Frobenius squares commute as maps of the coefficient diagrams, before a Weil isomorphism on an input is chosen. The inputs supplied by integral representatives and the integral dualizing object are in the finite-Tor domains: [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] supplies the uniform Tor condition, and [prop-coef-integral-dualizing] supplies both the integral dualizing object and its finite reductions. To pass these identities through completion use the simultaneous enhanced section models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], whose statement includes pullback, coefficient tensor, evaluation, mates and their coherence, and says that taking transposes preserves these constructions. Inverse image for a scheme isomorphism is exact and preserves products and limits by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]; hence it commutes with the differentials and $1-s$ in the shifted product-cone construction of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Applying this functor to the coherent coefficient diagrams therefore preserves their commuting squares, and then rationalization preserves them. The cofinal exponents are $en$, not $n$ at both coefficient fields. This proves Frobenius compatibility of the scalar tensor and compact-support coefficient comparisons used to transpose adjunction data; it does not infer equality of integral maps merely from equality of unrelated finite reductions.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, first three sentences: coherent coefficient comparisons and normalized tower passage

proof.text:
The scalar-compatible identifications of [lem-coef-rational-operations] preserve the actual adjunction units and counits. Its dualizing comparison $u:T_{L/E}\omega_{X,E}\to\omega_{X,L}$ is consequently characterized by the scalar-extended compact-support counit. Taking its adjunction transpose after Frobenius in the two orders gives the same counit composite: Step 6 supplies compatibility of scalar tensor and compact support with the Frobenius square, and Step 3 supplies equivariance of the counit. Uniqueness of transpose therefore gives
$$u\,\theta_{T\omega_E}=\theta_{\omega_L}P_X(u).$$
The integral comparisons of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension], rationalized in [thm-coef-rational-verdier], give $\beta_K:T_{L/E}D_EK\to D_L(T_{L/E}K)$. Their evaluation compatibility characterizes $\beta_K$ by
$$e^L_{TK}(1\otimes\beta_K)=u\,T(e^E_K)\,t_{K,D_EK}^{-1},$$
where $t:T(K\otimes D_EK)\to TK\otimes TD_EK$ is the scalar tensor comparison. Apply $P_X$ to this equation. In the two resulting routes use Step 4 for $e^E_K,e^L_{TK}$, the equation just proved for $u$, and Step 6 for $t$. Both routes transpose to the same equivariant pairing, so the transpose bijection of Step 5 [lem-coef-completed-tensor-hom-transpose], at the field $L$, gives
$$\beta_K\theta_{TD_EK}=\theta_{D_L(TK)}P_X(\beta_K).$$
The comparison between $P_XT$ and $TP_X$ is the pullback scalar isomorphism of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] followed by rationalization. Its formation is the same coefficient tensor construction of Step 6. Naturality of $\beta$ applies to arbitrary rational $\theta_K^{-1}$, not just integral morphisms. The evaluation, biduality and adjunction compatibility diagrams of [thm-coef-rational-verdier, lem-coef-rational-operations] now have equivariant edges; their existing equalities are therefore equalities in the faithful pair categories. Inverses, identities and composites of equivariant arrows are equivariant by substitution in the defining equation.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: rationalized dualizing, evaluation, biduality and adjunction comparisons

proof.text: Finally use the precise common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. If a $\Qlb$-Weil object has underlying pair $(E,K)$, its structure map and inverse each have a representative over some finite field. Choose a common overfield for those representatives; since each of the two inverse equations holds in the colimit Hom group, enlarge once for each equation. Over the resulting finite field both equations hold, so the representative is an actual isomorphism $P_XK_L\to K_L$. The same finite procedure represents any Weil morphism and its equivariance equation. The functor formulas of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] identify the pullbacks, tensors and internal Homs of these representatives. Apply Steps 1–7 at that field. Their compatibility under enlargement (Step 7) makes all the resulting structures and maps independent of the representative. The underlying descended duality and exceptional adjunction, with the same evaluation and biduality, are exactly [thm-coef-qbar-verdier]. A finite collection of maps and equations, including any scalar-extension compatibility diagram, is handled by the same common-field construction. Thus every assertion holds at $\Qlb$. Throughout, $\theta_K$ and its inverse were used as morphisms in the rational category. For example at a point multiplication by $\varpi_E$ on $E$ is a valid Weil isomorphism, despite not preserving any lattice isomorphically; the construction gives multiplication by $\varpi_E^{-1}$ on its dual. No Frobenius-stable integral lattice has been used.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, last two sentences: one common finite field and no integral Weil lattice
